fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. John says many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in Him (John 11:45). They didn't just watch a dead man walk out of the tomb and shrug (John 11:44). Believing is where this whole passage starts, and it's the part I like best.

Not this time, friend. John says plainly that many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in Him (John 11:45). Some of them did go off and tell the Pharisees, but that's the next verse (John 11:46). Verse 45 says many believed.
That's it, baker. The council says, "This man is performing many signs." (John 11:47) Notice what they don't say. They don't argue that the signs didn't happen. I think that has them worried.

Sabbath trouble does come up with Jesus in other places, like John 5:16, but not in this verse. Here the council asks, "What are we to do?" and then says, "This man is performing many signs." (John 11:47) The signs are what they name about Jesus in this meeting. The Sabbath never comes up.

Good guess for a council meeting, but it's not what they say. Their words are, "This man is performing many signs." (John 11:47) Moses never comes up in this passage. The signs are what they name about Jesus here.

Right, friend. The council says, "…everyone will believe in Him, and then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation." (John 11:48) That's what they say they're afraid of. The Romans were the empire that ruled the land back then (Luke 3:1).

The Greeks are a fair guess, but the council doesn't name them. They say, "…then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation." (John 11:48) Romans were the empire that ruled the land back then (Luke 3:1). The council's worry is about them.

Egypt shows up all over the Bible, but not in this verse. The council says, "…then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation." (John 11:48) The Romans were the empire in charge at this time (Luke 3:1). That's who the council has on its mind.

The Romans do come up back in verse 48, but not like this. There the council says they're afraid the Romans "…will come and take away both our place and our nation." (John 11:48) Here, Jesus would die for the scattered children of God "…to gather them together into one." (John 11:52) John doesn't mention freeing anyone from the Romans in this verse.

That's the one, baker. Jesus withdrew "…to a town called Ephraim in an area near the wilderness. And He stayed there with the disciples." (John 11:54) John says that's the result of the plot, so Jesus stepped out of public view. Ephraim, out by the wilderness, with the disciples right beside Him.

Not quite, friend. The people are asking each other, "What do you think? Will He come to the feast at all?" (John 11:56) That sounds like wondering to me, not being sure. I think they really couldn't say.
